item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FAY MOVING SLOWLY SOUTHWARD... As of 3:00 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 the center of Fay was located near 33.3, -32.0 with movement S at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1000 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
598 
WTNT31 KNHC 211451
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026
 
...FAY MOVING SLOWLY SOUTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM GMT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.3N 32.0W
ABOUT 430 MI...690 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...S OR 180 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 33.3 North, longitude 32.0 West.  Fay is 
moving toward the south near 5 mph (7 km/h).  A gradual turn toward 
the southwest and west-southwest is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued weakening is forecast, and Fay could
degenerate to a post-tropical remnant low in a couple of days.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 211452
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026

Fay continues to be affected by strong west-northwesterly vertical 
wind shear.  Practically all of the deep convection is confined to 
a band of showers and thunderstorms located well to the 
east of the well-defined low-level center.  Using a blend of 
subjective and objective intensity estimates, the advisory 
intensity is reduced to 45 kt.

Global model simulations show a strong upper-level trough shifting 
eastward from Fay during the next day or two.  This evolution would 
allow for some relaxation of the shear, and this is also indicated 
by the Decay SHIPS model.  However, the model guidance also 
indicates that the system is likely to encounter a drier low- to 
mid-level air mass, which should inhibit re-strengthening.  
Simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF output shows Fay's deep 
convection mostly dissipated during the next few days.  Therefore 
the official forecast, like the previous one, shows the cyclone 
degenerating into a remnant low by 48 hours.

Fay is now moving southward at around 4 kt, along the eastern side 
of a mid-level high.  Over the next several days, the cyclone 
is expected turn southwestward to west-southwestward and move 
around the southeastern and southern periphery of the high.  This 
should keep the system over the open Atlantic through dissipation 
later in the week.  Not much change has been made to the previous 
NHC track forecast, which remains in good agreement with the Google 
DeepMind ensemble mean and corrected model consensus, HCCA.
